items.id: function:MIXED LOGIC EXPRESSION ( ... ) WITH !, AND, OR
items.keyword: Mixed logic expression ( ... ) with !, AND, OR
items.summary: Parenthesised expressions mixing arithmetic, relational and logical operators with numeric and boolean data; '!' is NOT.
notes: A mixed-logic IF needs the comma before its action: IF (DI[1]),JMP LBL[1] - without it the line is rejected (ASBN-092).
Priority: ! > * / DIV MOD > + - > relational > AND > OR. Position and palletizing data not allowed. ~20 items max. GRAMMAR BUG: '!' inside the line is taken as start of a comment.

examples: 11: FORCE CTRL[1: Start Contouring] : ErrorLBL[0] ;// Start Contouring
items.summary: Runs force-controlled motion (push, face match, insert, search, contouring...) using the parameters of the given force control schedule; on error it can jump to an error label for recovery.
notes: ErrorLBL[n] is required: FORCE CTRL[1] alone is rejected. The controller stores the label on a continuation line (FORCE CTRL[1:] then : ErrorLBL[0]).

The manual names the instruction 'FORCE CTRL' and says it has two parts: the force schedule number and an error label number (second line). The actual pendant/LS rendering is only in figures (Fig 4-5, 7-2, 7-3, 7-11) that did not survive text extraction, so the exact bracket/error-label spelling is NOT confirmed.
Error label 0 = program stops on the error instead of jumping. For Contouring / Contouring End the error label must be 0 (no jump possible).

Schedule function types (chosen in the force schedule, not in the TP line): Unused, Constant Push, Face Match, Shaft Insert, Groove Insert, Square Insert, Phase Match Ins. (Phase Match Insert), Ins. Phase Match (Insertion Phase Match), Search, Phase Search, Hole Search, Clutch Search (and Clutch Insert, mentioned in passing), Contouring, Contouring End, Threading.
Contouring is started by a FORCE CTRL with a 'Contouring' schedule and ended by a FORCE CTRL with a 'Contouring End' schedule.

items.summary: Runs the spot weld sequence for one gun: optional backup state and equalization pressure before the weld, valve pressure, weld schedule, then equalization pressure and backup state after the weld. Usually on a FINE motion line; can also be its own line.
notes: On a V9.40 SpotTool+ servo-gun controller the loader keeps only SPOT[S=n] (plus ANTIC=): SPOT[BU=*,P=M,S=2,BU=*] is stored as SPOT[S=2], on a continuation line after the motion. The BU/EP/P fields belong to other gun types.
Which fields appear depends on Spot Config: P only with multiple valve pressure, BU only with backups, EP only with equalization pressure enabled.
BU before the weld: C=close, *=unchanged; BU after: O=open, *=unchanged. EP: H/M/L or 0-31 binary encoded; P: H/M/L or 0-15 binary encoded.
The equipment number comes from the program header (Equip#).

Syntax line shows double quotes, examples use single quotes (TP string literal).

items.summary: Macro that selects the Lincoln Production Monitoring weld profile; placed before the Arc Start or Weld Start.
notes: With multi-equipment there is one macro per equipment (SET_PM_PROF_E1, _E2, ...).
One example shows 'SET_PM_PROF[1];' with square brackets, probably a typo.
The alternative is the parameter instruction $AWELEPM[eq].$WP_NUM = n.

items.summary: Predefined SpotTool+ macro instructions (programs clr_tran, ENTR1ZON, EXIT1ZON, SAFEZONE, mov_home, mov_repr, atpounce, opnclmer, repos_cl, req_cont, set-segm, ver_decn, GET_PART) for PLC interlocks, interference zones and home moves.

items.summary: Displays a read-only status screen (registers, I/O, variables, time...) refreshed every second, then continues.
notes: These are macro programs installed by Menu Utility, so 'macro call' is the right classification; the extension simply does not know the names (multi-word, with a parenthesised argument list). Manual uses curly quotes; real .LS uses straight single quotes.
Menus stored in MENU4nn.VR.
